prompt.context: Our client, High Q Plastics, is an automotive parts supplier in the U.S. They primarily manufacture and sell plastic injection-molded parts, such as grills, door handles, and decorative trim, to automotive customers. The client has two primary revenue sources: large automotive OEMs and aftermarket. The client has recently seen declining profits, primarily due to increased price competition from new overseas competitors in China. Annual profits have declined from $50M to $20M over the past few years.
prompt.question: What is the reason behind declining profitability? How can High Q improve profits? Can they reach $100M in profits by 2014?

clarifying_info.q: What is the overall trend in automotive sales?
clarifying_info.a: Automotive sales overall are still growing steadily, driven by emerging markets.

clarifying_info.q: Is automotive manufacturing staying in the U.S.?
clarifying_info.a: Automotive manufacturing is leaving the U.S.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's competitive position?
clarifying_info.a: The client is currently one of the leaders in this category.

clarifying_info.q: Where is the client's manufacturing based?

clarifying_info.a: Revenues have been slowly declining over the last 5 years.

clarifying_info.q: How does client quality compare to Chinese competitors?
clarifying_info.a: The client's products are of higher quality than most Chinese competitors' products.
Automotive OEM customers are looking to reduce cost, driving increased price competition among parts suppliers.

exhibits.title: High Q's 2010 Financials, By Facility
exhibits.shows: A table showing 2010 revenues, labor costs, material costs, overhead costs, and net profits for each of four U.S. plants (Plant A, B, C, D).

exhibits.title: 2010 U.S. Automotive Market
exhibits.shows: A pie chart of 2010 U.S. automotive sales by vehicle segment, with a note on total market size.

exhibits.title: U.S. Automotive OEM Market — Truck/SUV Market Share 2010 vs. 2014
exhibits.shows: A grouped bar chart showing each major OEM's share of the truck and SUV segment in 2010 and 2014 (predicted), plus additional supply data for High Q's relationship with Toyota.

data.additional: High Q supplies 70% of Toyota's business; Avg. price of High Q products sold to Toyota = $20

framework: Industry dynamics: Analyze sales volume trends; assess OEM vs. aftermarket segment size, growth, and profitability
Competitors: Identify who the new Chinese competitors are, their relative market share, pricing, and cost structure; assess technology/quality advantage
Revenue: Examine how client prices have changed; determine whether declines are across all customers and products
Costs: Identify trends in cost structure — rising labor, rising material, or overhead inefficiencies

questions.prompt: What key questions would you ask an industry expert to understand the reasons behind High Q's declining profits?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure questions along four MECE buckets: (1) Industry — volume trends, OEM vs. aftermarket mix and profitability; (2) Competitors — who they are, market share, pricing, cost structure, quality/technology differentiation; (3) Revenue — client price trends across customers and products; (4) Costs — trends in labor, material, and overhead. Strong answers cover all four buckets with specific, answerable questions.

questions.prompt: The CEO wants to know if $100M in annual profits is achievable by 2014. What would you need to know, and what data would you ask for?
questions.guidance: Candidate should state that profit = Q*(P - VC) - FC, so you need: annual unit volume (Q), selling price (P), variable cost per unit (VC: labor and material), and fixed costs (FC: overhead). This sets up the profitability model needed for Q4.

steps: Identify variable costs per unit (labor + material per unit)
Compute contribution margin and subtract fixed costs
math.answer: Framework answer only — specific numbers come from Exhibit 1 in Q4.

questions.prompt: What ways can you think of to increase revenues? What ways can you think of to reduce costs?
questions.guidance: Candidate should generate 2-3 concrete ideas for each. Cost reduction: find alternative/cheaper material sources; invest in process automation to reduce labor; consolidate manufacturing sites to cut SG&A; relocate closer to customers to cut transportation costs. Revenue growth: segment customers by price sensitivity; increase marketing in the aftermarket segment; negotiate long-term contracts with OEM customers.

questions.prompt: The client plans lean manufacturing across all 4 U.S. plants. They expect to produce 80% of 2010 volumes in 2014 and reduce prices by 10% due to competition. Lean manufacturing will save an additional 20% on raw materials and 30% on labor. What is the change in profits from 2010 to 2014?
questions.guidance: Candidate must apply the volume/price reduction to revenues, then apply two-step cost reductions to labor and material (volume effect first, then lean savings), while keeping overhead fixed. Should note that even with lean manufacturing the CEO's $100M target is far out of reach, and should flag the importance of managing client expectations. Plant D is a concern due to its disproportionately high overhead.

math.setup: 2014 figures per plant: Revenue = 2010 Revenue * 0.80 (volume) * 0.90 (price). Labor = 2010 Labor * 0.80 (volume) * 0.70 (lean). Material = 2010 Material * 0.80 (volume) * 0.80 (lean). Overhead = unchanged.
steps: Overhead unchanged: A=20, B=15, C=15, D=30
Net Profit per plant = Revenue - Labor - Material - Overhead
math.answer: Total 2014 profits = $28M; additional profits vs. 2010 = $8M. The $100M target is not achievable.

questions.prompt: Toyota is predicted to achieve a 30% increase in truck and SUV market share by 2014 (from 10% to 40% per Exhibit 3). Based on Exhibits 2 and 3, what additional profits can High Q expect from this shift?
questions.guidance: Candidate should work from total market size to Toyota's unit sales, then apply High Q's supply share and price to compute revenues in 2010 and 2014. The profit impact question asks for additional revenue; the case solution treats all additional revenue as profits for this step (or the interviewer may accept rounded answers of $13M or $14M).

math.setup: U.S. Truck & SUV market = Total U.S. Autos * Trucks & SUVs share. Toyota Truck & SUV sales = that market * Toyota share. High Q qty sold to Toyota = Toyota sales * 70% supply share. High Q revenue from Toyota = qty * $20 per unit.
steps: High Q qty sold to Toyota 2010: 320,000 * 70% = 224,000
Toyota Truck & SUV sales 2014: 3,200,000 * 40% = 1,280,000 (assuming flat total market)
High Q qty sold to Toyota 2014: 1,280,000 * 70% = 896,000
math.answer: Additional revenue from Toyota's market share gain = ~$13.4M (rounded answers of $13M or $14M are acceptable).

brainstorming.prompt: What additional opportunities exist to increase High Q's profits over the next few years beyond lean manufacturing?

categories.name: Cost Reduction
ideas: Find alternative/cheaper material sources to lower COGS
Invest in process automation to structurally reduce labor costs
Consolidate the 4 manufacturing plants, especially Plant D which has disproportionately high overhead costs
Relocate manufacturing closer to OEM customers to cut transportation costs

categories.name: Revenue Growth
ideas: Segment OEM customers by price sensitivity and tailor pricing accordingly
Increase marketing and sales effort in the aftermarket segment, which may be less price-competitive
Negotiate long-term supply contracts with OEM customers to lock in volumes
Pursue growth in plastic injection-molded parts for non-automotive industries with less price competition

categories.name: Strategic Moves
ideas: Diversify into other industries to reduce dependence on automotive OEMs
Leverage quality advantage over Chinese competitors as a differentiator in premium segments
Pursue partnerships or acquisitions to gain scale advantages

recommendation: High Q should proceed with lean manufacturing implementation across all 4 plants, which will increase total profits from $20M to $28M (+$8M)
The CEO's $100M profit target by 2014 is not achievable under current plans; client expectations must be reset
High Q should simultaneously pursue the Toyota opportunity (~$13M additional revenue from Toyota's rising truck/SUV market share) and invest in aftermarket segment growth
risks: Lean manufacturing implementation may face operational disruption across all 4 plants simultaneously
Continued loss of OEM volume if price competition intensifies beyond the 10% assumed reduction
Overhead-heavy Plant D ($30M overhead on $72M revenue) remains a structural drag on profitability
next_steps: Evaluate consolidation of Plant D into other facilities to eliminate high overhead burden
Develop a dedicated aftermarket sales and marketing strategy
Explore diversification into non-automotive plastic injection molding to reduce concentration risk
Align with CEO on realistic profit targets and a 3-5 year roadmap
